name: Nextdoor

sources.title: Nextdoor for Business — free Business Page: claim flow, eligibility, posting to neighborhood newsfeed

requirements: You must be an owner, employee, or authorized representative of the business
Local businesses, casual service providers, and home service providers are eligible

Casual goods/services providers (e.g., dog walking, babysitting) need official business documents to verify the page before posting to the neighborhood newsfeed; without documents they can only use 'Neighbor Made'/'Neighbor Services' options from a member account
Business Pages may already exist (data comes from third-party public sources) — search by name + location before creating a new page
preparation: Business name, category, service area, contact info, photos
A Nextdoor account — either a new business account or your existing personal member account to link
Business verification documents if you're a casual/home service provider
workflow: Go to business.nextdoor.com/local and choose 'Sign up for Free' / 'Claim Your Free Business Page'
Create an account or log in (optionally link your personal Nextdoor account — don't link if employees will share the business login)
Search for your business by name + location; claim the existing page, or click 'Not here? Create your Business Page.'
Complete the page: contact info, photos, story
Post to the neighborhood newsfeed from the Content tab ('Create Post or Local Deal'); choose audience radius/neighborhoods
watchFor: If you don't select your own neighborhood for a post, you won't see it from your member account
Duplicate pages are common because pages are auto-generated — always search before creating
Nextdoor is a local neighborhood network: best fit for local services, not global SaaS launches
Verification documents are required before casual providers can post to the newsfeed
countsAsLive: The claimed Business Page is publicly visible on nextdoor.com with correct name/info, and (if posting) your posts appear in the selected neighborhoods' feeds
unknowns: Exact verification document types accepted for casual providers
Whether Business Pages are publicly indexable by search engines or login-gated
